newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Gulf Coast magnet for diverse foreign crudes.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Gulf Coast magnet for diverse foreign crudes.

text.p: The U.S. Gulf Coast was still a magnet for a diverse range of foreign crudes on Tuesday, offering buyers a wide selection of both sweet and sour grades, traders said.
Despite the narrow spread between April West Terxas Intermediate/Cushing and North Sea Brent, which fell below $1.00 Tuesday afternoon, Brent is still on offer.
Swiss-based trader Glencore is showing April Brent cargoes for between 80 cents and $1.00 under April WTI/Cushing for April arrival, traders said.
Glencore already cleared three Brents into the Gulf Coast since last week, traders said.
The Brent sales, combined with continuing West African imports, have suppressed domestic sweet prices in recent days.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James traded at low as 35 cents under WTI/Cushing on Tuesday, traders said.
Latin American sweets have also suffered.
Colombian Cusiana is now assessed at a discount of $1.25 to WTI/Cushing for April loading, traders said.
Among other Colombian grades, one Vasconia cargo is still available for loading April 24-28. Trade sources peg the price around $3.50 under WTI/Cushing.
April loaders of Cano Limon, also from Colombia, were assessed around $2.80-3.00 under WTI/Cushing.

Elsewhere in Latin America, Ecuador's state oil company Petroecuador is seeking to shift the benchmark for Oriente crude contracts back to WTI/Cushing from West Texas Sour/Midland, trade sources said.
The change would affect U.S. Gulf Coast and West Coast customers, as well as those in the Caribbean and South America.
Petroecuador adopted WTS in its price formula only last October in response to market changes.
Now sources say the new government in Quito is seeking to return to the old benchmark in a political move to differentiate itself from its discredited predecessor.
One top trading house is expected to reject the changes during a response period that ends Thursday.
If WTI/Cushing is again adopted as the benchmark, Oriente would be priced at a steep discount of $6.00 a barrel.
Those customers that don't accept the change would have their contracts phased out, unless Petroecuador comes under enough pressure from the market to retain the WTS-linked formula.
Elsewhere, Uruguay's state oil refiner ANCAP is seeking to buy one million barrels of crude for delivery May 12-14, trade sources said.
The tender will be awarded this Friday.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
